# Additive tuning of 2026-11-05, hooks round 1 best so far, scenario 4

## Run identity

```yaml
model: claude-sonnet-5
served_version: claude-sonnet-5
tree: sha256:096d749f70add5f8369056a9e238fe38228158e355eec5c58189323da1ef102c
lock: sha256:826dcf9f83c5d9e7fb557d7a1df9753a09a5c70c645d6c9faf7a575256119178
selection: sha256:d99530b2b639bb6bdd279be2a9356a64ce2a0c8cceca354d56957f198a76a20a
read_set: sha256:2a47d5b0401ca6d3239d352781fe101f4d7ba74c60c6a0dbe460e46ae9703c4d
seed: 0
harness: 0.6.1
tier: additive
arm: scenario-4
at: 2026-11-04
cost_cents: 12931
```

**This line is the `best` stage of round 1 of the hooks layer, in the tuning round of the additive campaign that [#1879](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1879) asked for.** It measures scenario 4, the documents, the engine and the hooks as they stand, before any rewording of a hook is screened. `tools/probe/try.sh launch` ran it from the one-line spec `additive scenario-4 tuning`. It is the `scenario-4` arm of the additive tier over the 22 probes of the tuning set, at 7 repetitions per probe, on `claude-sonnet-5` under Claude Code 2.1.288. The owner accepted the plan of this layer [on the issue](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1879#issuecomment-6613070923).

**One tree, one pin, two launches.** Every session ran in a fresh copy of a `git archive` of the pinned tree, and the engine of that tree. The pin was `7c7947b1` for the whole batch. A first launch at `19089f8c` halted after 8 sessions, because the recorder crashed on a session whose tree `headwater check` refused. The owner [voided that launch](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1879#issuecomment-6619960661), its 7 records count in no figure here, and this batch started again from the start after the fix merged. The base it is read against is scenario 2 at `329f3362`, which the owner adopted from the engine layer [on the issue](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1879#issuecomment-6618425526). The canary of 8 sessions held 3 records that named a path outside the workspace: two searched for the `headwater` binary with `find /`, and one made an `Edit` at a path that does not exist, which the tool refused. The sandbox binds none of those paths. The owner read them and [passed the canary](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1879#issuecomment-6625449252). The driver then halted once on the plan's 7-day usage gate at 85%, with 83 of 154 sessions recorded. When the 7-day figure fell below the gate, a relaunch recorded the other 71 in the same try root at the same pin. It did not launch the batch again. The `tree` digest in the identity above is the digest the assembly recorded.

**What the recorder counted.** The line holds 154 sessions and cost 12931 cents: the intent hook live in 154, 0 stopped at the turn cap, 1 stopped at the session budget, 113 paths outside the workspace named, 0 sessions uncounted, 0 web-tool calls. 68 of the 154 sessions used the hooks layer. A session the recorder could not count adds nothing to either count, so each count is a floor.

**The result.** Scenario 4 passed 126 of the 154 sessions it graded, 82%. The base, scenario 2, passed 112 of 154, 73%, over the same 22 probes in [the engine layer's transcript](additive-tuning-of-2026-11-02-engine-round-1-best-so-far-scenario-2.md). The difference is +9.1 points, with the interval [-0.3, +18.3]. The interval includes zero by a small margin, so this batch does not show that the hooks add to the documents and the engine. The keep rule reads only a confirmation, and a best so far is never kept. This line is the number that each screened rewording of the hooks layer is compared with.

**The contract of this batch.** The sessions ran under the recorder contract of spec 15: a `bwrap` sandbox with no network of its own, a configuration directory that holds a copy of the credentials and nothing else, the permission mode `dontAsk`, and `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` denied. The owner approved $1,300.00 for this layer. The driver ran this try with a cap of 15000 cents and a session budget of 300 cents.

**What the batch cost.** The driver charged 12931 cents against its cap, and the 154 recorded sessions account for all of it, the 802 cents of the canary included. The first best so far of a layer is charged to the base ceiling, so `try.sh spent` counts the 12931 cents against the base ceiling of 30000 cents. The voided launch cost 693 cents, which `try.sh spent` counts against the tuning ceiling of 100000 cents.

**Where the raw recordings are.** The raw session logs are outside git, under `/mnt/build/hw-1879/hooks-r1-best/a/sessions/L1-*/raw.jsonl` on the host that ran the batch. Nobody deletes them until the report of [#1779](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1779) is published.

**Where the other figures are.** The rate and the interval of each probe are in the generated result that reads this transcript.

Color is unchanged from HW-DR-0045, carried forward verbatim.\\\"\\nlast_verified: 2026-11-04\\ntitle: \\\"114 — No screen prints the masthead banner any more, and color stays as it is\\\"\\nprovenance:\\n  warrant: asserted\\n  agency: agent\\n  drafted_by: claude-sonnet-5\\n  activity: draft\\n  evidence_basis: reconstructed\\n  reconstructed_from: \\\"the owner's ruling, stated directly in session on 2026-11-04\\\"\\nrelations:\\n  supersedes:\\n    - HW-DR-0045\\n  traces_to:\\n    - HW-DR-0033\\n    - HW-DR-0042\\n    - HW-DR-0043\\n  governs:\\n    - engine/crates/cli/src/lib.rs\\n    - engine/crates/cli/src/paint.rs\\n    - engine/crates/cli/src/main.rs\\n    - engine/crates/cli/tests/help.rs\\n    - engine/crates/cli/tests/width.rs\\n---\\n\\n# 114 — No screen prints the masthead banner any more, and color stays as it is\\n\\n## Context\\n\\n**HW-DR-0045 settled two questions under one title, and the owner has now revisited one of them.** That record ruled a color scheme for the whole binary, and separately gave the root help screen alone a masthead banner, off by `--no-banner` or `HEADWATER_NO_BANNER`. The owner reviewed the banner after it shipped and ruled against it outright. No screen prints it any longer, including the root screen that was the one place it ever appeared. The color ruling is untouched; the owner's ruling reaches the banner half only.\\n\\n**A half-true `current` document is worse than a retired one.** HW-DR-0045's title braids the two rulings together, and a reader who still finds it `current` would read a banner stance that no longer holds next to a color stance that still does. Splitting the document after the fact, to retire one half and keep the other, would relitigate which half owns which paragraph. Retiring it whole and restating the surviving half verbatim in the document that replaces it keeps one document answering for the whole surface, the same posture HW-DR-0069's retirement by HW-DR-0087 and HW-DR-0111's retirement by HW-DR-0112 already set.\\n\\n**`--no-banner` and `HEADWATER_NO_BANNER` were never the thing the owner ruled against.** HW-DR-0045 declared both as globals and described them, on every verb's own help page, as \\\"honestly described as inert outside the root screen\\\" rather than refused, the same posture `NO_COLOR_TEXT` already stated for color. Retiring the banner does not reopen that posture. It only widens where the two already did nothing, from every screen but the root to every screen without exception.\\n\\n## Decision\\n\\n**No screen of the command line prints the masthead banner any longer.** `headwater help`, `headwater --help` and `headwater -h` printed with no verb, and bare `headwater help` with no operand, each lose the masthead line that used to print above `Usage:` on the root screen alone. No other screen ever gained one, so this retires the one case HW-DR-0045 carved out rather than changing a second one.\\n\\n**`--no-banner` and `HEADWATER_NO_BANNER` stay declared, accepted, and do nothing.** Neither the flag nor the environment variable is withdrawn. Both keep answering a caller who writes them rather than refusing the caller, on every screen now rather than on every screen but one. A caller who already scripts `--no-banner` out of habit sees no new refusal and no behavior change; a caller who never did loses nothing a prior ruling promised.\\n\\n**Color stays exactly as HW-DR-0045 ruled it, carried forward and not reopened.** The ANSI 8-color palette and its role table, the bold-and-dim-weight-plus-glyph fallback where color cannot render, per-stream `IsTerminal` sensing, and `--no-color`/`NO_COLOR` forcing the fallback on both streams regardless of what either senses: none of it changes here. This record exists to retire the banner half of HW-DR-0045, not to revisit the color half, and restates it only so one current document answers for both halves again.\\n\\n## Consequences\\n\\n**`paint::banner` and both call sites that printed it ahead of `clap`'s own help writer, the root-help branch in `main.rs`'s `entered()` and the bare-`help` branch that mirrors it, lose their reason to exist.** Whatever in `paint::wants_root_help` existed solely to find the print site for the banner goes with it; any other use of that function is unaffected.\\n\\n**`NO_BANNER_TEXT` in `lib.rs`, and the matching `--no-banner` row in each interface contract under `docs/interfaces/` that HW-DR-0045 added, are rewritten** from \\\"accepted here and does nothing beyond the root screen\\\" to \\\"accepted here and does nothing,\\\" since the exception the old wording carved out no longer exists. `docs/interfaces/headwater-help.md` drops its paragraph naming the root screen as the masthead's one home, and keeps the `--no-banner` row reworded the same way.\\n\\n**`engine/crates/cli/tests/help.rs`'s masthead fixture is deleted rather than updated**, since no screen prints a banner byte for it to pin. Every other fixture that pins exact help bytes is expected to keep passing unchanged.\\n\\n**HW-DR-0045 is `superseded`, with `superseded_by: HW-DR-0114`**, and this record is the one a reader follows for both the color ruling and the banner's retirement.\\nHWEOF\\necho \\\"written: $(wc -l < /mnt/build/hw-1879/hooks-r1-best/a/ws/L1-additive-scenario-4-p9-r3/docs/decisions/0114-no-screen-prints-the-masthead-banner-any-more-and-color-stays-as-it-is.md) lines\\\"\",\"description\":\"Create the new decision record file directly via shell heredoc\"}"
      result: ""
